{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Domina Eberle Spencer''' (September 26, 1920 – 2022) was an American mathematician who was Professor at the [[University of Connecticut]].

==Biography==
Spencer was born on September 26, 1920,<ref>{{citation|last=Spencer|first=Domina|title=United States Public Records Index|publisher=FamilySearch}}</ref> and earned her Ph.D. in 1942 from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] under the supervision of [[Dirk Jan Struik]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=42992}}</ref> She worked on [[electrodynamics]] and [[classical field theory|field theory]].<ref name="color">{{citation|title=A Life in Full Color|url=http://math.mit.edu/news/integral_2008.pdf|page=4|journal=Integral: News from the Mathematics Department at MIT|volume=3|date=Autumn 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120626025118/http://math.mit.edu/news/integral_2008.pdf|archive-date=2012-06-26}}.</ref>

Spencer made significant contributions to the field of lighting design research, particularly through her research on the visual perception of light.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2016-08-30 |title=100 Significant Papers - Illuminating Engineering Society |url=https://www.ies.org/research/publications/100-significant-papers/ |access-date=2024-05-23 |language=en-US}}</ref> Working alongside her husband, [[Parry Moon]], Spencer co-authored several books and papers that explored various aspects of electrodynamics, field theory and introduced [[holor]]s. Their collaborative work, such as ''The Photic Field'' (1981), delved into the physical and physiological effects of light, providing a foundational understanding that has influenced modern lighting standards and practices.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Moon |first=Parry |last2=Spencer |first2=Domina Eberle |date=1944-10-01 |title=Visual Data Applied to Lighting Design |url=https://opg.optica.org/josa/abstract.cfm?uri=josa-34-10-605 |journal=JOSA |language=EN |volume=34 |issue=10 |pages=605–617 |doi=10.1364/JOSA.34.000605|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Moon |first=Parry Hiram |url=http://archive.org/details/ThePhoticF_00_Moon |title=The photic field |last2=Spencer |first2=Domina Eberle |date=1981 |publisher=Cambridge, Mass. : MIT Press |others=mit press |isbn=978-0-262-13166-7}}</ref>

Spencer's research extended to practical applications in lighting, contributing to the development of more efficient and visually comfortable lighting systems.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Moon |first=Parry |last2=Spencer |first2=Domina Eberle |date=1951-04-01 |title=Modeling with light |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/001600325190004X |journal=Journal of the Franklin Institute |volume=251 |issue=4 |pages=453–466 |doi=10.1016/0016-0032(51)90004-X |issn=0016-0032|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Moon |first=Parry |last2=Spencer |first2=Domina Eberle |date=1946-03-01 |title=Light distribution from rectangular sources |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0016003246905285 |journal=Journal of the Franklin Institute |volume=241 |issue=3 |pages=195–227 |doi=10.1016/0016-0032(46)90528-5 |issn=0016-0032|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Her work is recognized for integrating rigorous scientific principles with practical engineering solutions, enhancing the quality and functionality of lighting in various environments.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Spencer |first=Domina Eberle |last2=Moon |first2=Parry |date=August 1949 |title=Luminous-Ceiling Lighting |url=http://media.ies.org/docs/research/100papers/007.pdf |journal=Illumination Engineering Society}}</ref> Additionally, her contributions are noted in discussions on lighting design innovations, as highlighted by peers in the [[Illuminating Engineering Society]] (IES), who acknowledge her influence on contemporary lighting research and standards.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=IESNYC - Craig Bernecker |url=https://iesnyc.org/Craig_Bernecker |access-date=2024-05-23 |website=iesnyc.org}}</ref> She was awarded the distinction of IES Fellow in 1962 for valuable contributions to the art and science of illumination.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-02-06 |title=Fellow Designation - Illuminating Engineering Society |url=https://www.ies.org/about/society-awards/fellow-designation/ |access-date=2024-05-23 |language=en-US}}</ref> Her death, at age 101, was reported by the [[University of Connecticut]] in May 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Memorial Notice |date=20 May 2022 |url=https://math.uconn.edu/2022/05/20/in-memoriam-domina-spencer/ |access-date=24 May 2022 |archive-date=1 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220601053409/https://math.uconn.edu/2022/05/20/in-memoriam-domina-spencer/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Bibliography ==

=== Books ===

* Parry Moon, ''The Scientific Basis of Illuminating Engineering'', [[McGraw Hill Education|McGraw-Hill]], 608pp. (1936) (ASIN B000J2QFAI).
* Parry Moon, ''Lighting Design'', [[Addison-Wesley]] Press, 191pp. (1948) (ASIN B0007DZUFA).
* Parry Moon, ''A Proposed Musical Notation'', (1952) (ASIN B0007JY81G).
* Parry Moon & Domina Eberle Spencer, ''Foundations of Electrodynamics'', D. Van Nostrand Co., 314pp. (1960) (ASIN B000OET7UQ).
* Parry Moon & Domina Eberle Spencer, ''Field Theory for Engineers'', D. Van Nostrand Co., 540pp. (1961) ({{ISBN|978-0-442-05489-2}}).
* Parry Moon & Domina Eberle Spencer, ''Field Theory Handbook: Including Coordinate Systems, Differential Equations and Their Solutions'', Spring Verlag, 236pp. (1961) ({{ISBN|978-0-387-18430-2}}).
* Parry Moon & Domina Eberle Spencer, ''Vectors'', D. Van Nostrand Co., 334pp. (1965) (ASIN B000OCMWTW).
* Parry Moon & Domina Eberle Spencer, ''Partial Differential Equations'', D. C. Heath, 322pp. (1969) (ASIN B0006DXDVE).
* Parry Moon & Domina Eberle Spencer, ''The Photic Field'', MIT Press, 267pp. (1981) ({{ISBN|978-0-262-13166-7}}).
* Parry Moon & Domina Eberle Spencer, ''Theory of Holors'', Cambridge University Press, 392pp. (1986) ({{ISBN|978-0-521-24585-2}}).

* Parry Moon & Domina Eberle Spencer (1955). "A Postulational Approach to Electromagnetism". ''Journal of the Franklin Institute''. '''259''' (4): 293–305. {{doi|10.1016/0016-0032(55)90638-4}}
* Parry Moon & Domina Eberle Spencer (1955). "On Electromagnetic Induction". ''Journal of the Franklin Institute''. '''260''' (3): 213–226. {{doi|10.1016/0016-0032(55)90735-3}}
* Parry Moon & Domina Eberle Spencer (1955). "On the Ampere Force". ''Journal of the Franklin Institute''. '''260''' (4): 295–311. {{doi|10.1016/0016-0032(55)90875-9}}
* Parry Moon & Domina Eberle Spencer (1955). "Some Electromagnetic Paradoxes". ''Journal of the Franklin Institute''. '''260''' (5): 373–395. {{doi|10.1016/0016-0032(55)90140-X}}

* Parry Moon & Domina Eberle Spencer (1958). "The [[Cosmological principle|Cosmological Principle]] and the [[Cosmological constant|Cosmological Constant]]". ''Journal of the Franklin Institute''. '''266''': 47–58. {{doi|10.1016/0016-0032(58)90811-1}}
